title: Artemisia annua – Solace Psychiatry
abstract:
- Purported Uses  
- Malaria
- Inflammation
- Cancer treatment
- Mechanism of Action  
Artemisinin, the active constituent of  
*A. annua*, exerts antimalarial effects by free radicals formed via cleavage of the endoperoxide bond in its structure, which are responsible for eradicating the*Plasmodium*species.[(23)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-23)  
Artemisinin induces apoptosis and cell cycle arrest of
Artemisinin induces apoptosis and cell cycle arrest of  
*Leishmani donovani*promastigotes. It has antiproliferative effects on medullary thyroid carcinoma cells[(8)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-8), and induces apoptosis in a lung cancer cell line by modulating p38 and calcium signaling[(2)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-2). In another study, it significantly inhibited cell growth and proliferation, and caused G1 cell-cycle arrest in neuroblastoma cell lines[(14)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-14). Dihydroartemisinin, a semi-synthetic derivative of artemisinin, demonstrates anti-inflammatory activity by attenuating COX-2 production via downregulation of serine/threonine kinase (AKT) and mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways[(25)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-25). Recent findings suggest that dihydroartemisinin-triggered apoptosis in colorectal cells occurs through the reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated mitochondria-dependent pathway[(24)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-24).[(26)](https://www.mskcc.org/cancer-care/integrative-medicine/herbs/artemisia-annua#references-26)
- Contraindications  
Patients with ulcers or gastrointestinal disorders should not take artemisia
